Tertiary: incremental validity must exceed 0.05 for at least four of the five alternatives. (iv)
Discriminant validity: the difference in Ψ(t) between full and ablated substrates must exceed
the 95th percentile of the same difference for the alternatives. (v) Convergent validity: the
time-to-degradation of Ψ(t) must be shorter than the alternatives by a preregistered ∆tmin.
Passing all criteria would establish that Ψ(t) is a measure of a physical property distinct from
thermal damage and metabolic cost, with additional predictive power. It would not establish
that Ψ(t) is a measure of phenomenal valence. The protocol is necessary but not sufficient.
6 The hard core
Postulate 2
The programme’s hard core is a metaphysical postulate, which we state explicitly.
Postulate 2 (dual-aspect monism of valence). The dynamical tension that
an integrated material system opposes to the violation of its own niche of thermo-
dynamic stability coincides ontologically, from the internal first-person perspective,
with primary affective valence.
Postulate 2 is not derived from the programme’s empirical hypotheses, and it is not falsifiable
at the level of qualia. If the postulate is false, the programme is not merely incomplete; it is
misdirected.
The conditional role
What the programme claims is the following. If Postulate 2 is true, then the five conditions of
§4 are necessary for primary interoceptive sentience, and the programme’s tests are informative
about the physical correlates of valence. If Postulate 2 is false, then the programme is a study of
a class of dissipative systems with certain organisational properties, and its tests are informative
about those properties, but not about sentience.
This is the most honest position the programme can adopt without abandoning the sentience
claim. The philosophical companion (Iavarone, 2026c) provides a three-stage argument for Pos-
tulate 2, summarised here because the programme’s claim to be about sentience, rather than
11

-- 11 of 17 --

v0.1, rev. 6 Necessary Conditions for Primary Interoceptive Sentience
about a class of dissipative systems, rests on it. (i) Structural isomorphism: valence and thermo-
dynamic tension share the same structure — directed, polar, temporally extended, relationally
structured, and action-guiding. (ii) Elimination: any ingredient that would distinguish valence
from tension is either physical, and hence already part of the tension, or non-physical, and hence
exposed to the standard objections against interactionist dualism. (iii) Parsimony: among the
available frameworks, dual-aspect monism is argued to leave the fewest unresolved problems.
The argument is an inference to the best explanation, not a proof. The companion engages
the standard objections (the conceivability argument, the knowledge argument, the explanatory
gap, and illusionism) and argues that none is decisive; the critical assessment of the corpus
(Iavarone, 2026e) regards these replies as standard and defeasible, and identifies four weaknesses
in the argument itself and a fifth in its classification (below). The isomorphism establishes
correspondence, not identity, and at one point assumes its conclusion; moreover, a bare structural
correspondence is cheap, since any collection with enough elements can be organised to have
a given structure (Kleiner, 2025), and the six features of the isomorphism are shared by any
setpoint regulator, a thermostat included. The elimination step does not address relational or
historical physical properties. On parsimony alone, illusionism is the more economical position.
The reply to the explanatory gap (a brute identity, like water and H2O) does not distinguish a
posteriori from a priori identity. The same assessment classifies the thermodynamic-phenomenal
gap as a structural limit of the programme: defended, not closed.
A further point concerns the label. In the literature, dual-aspect monism takes the physical
and the phenomenal to be aspects of the same underlying properties, and it has been developed
into explicitly panpsychist systems (Osborn, 2023). Views that attribute phenomenal or pro-
tophenomenal aspects to the constituents of matter, including the Russellian and neutral-monist
variants closely related to dual-aspect monism, face the combination problem (Chalmers, 2016).
Postulate 2 is narrower: it attributes the phenomenal aspect only to the tension of integrated,
self-maintaining systems, and the companion’s elimination argument reads as an a posteriori
identity thesis rather than as dual-aspect monism in the standard sense. The companion’s claim
that its position avoids the combination problem holds only for this restricted reading, and the
restriction to self-maintaining systems still requires a justification. The label is retained for
continuity across the corpus; the classification is examined in the critical assessment (Iavarone,
2026e).
What would strengthen or weaken the postulate
In favour. Independent philosophical arguments for dual-aspect monism. Convergence between
the physical correlates identified by the programme and those identified by independent theo-
ries. Empirical evidence that biological systems satisfying the five conditions exhibit valenced
behaviour robustly.
Against. Philosophical arguments for alternative metaphysical frameworks (emergentism, panpsy-
chism, dualism, illusionism). Failure of the programme’s necessary conditions to correlate with
independent measures of sentience in biological systems. Empirical evidence that the physi-
cal correlates identified by the programme dissociate from valence in cases where valence is
independently established.
7 Structural limits
The programme declares four structural limits that it does not commit to resolving within the
current framework.
1. Binding problem. The programme provides no account of how the substrate’s components
are unified into a single subject of experience. It addresses feature binding weakly and
12

-- 12 of 17 --

v0.1, rev. 6 Necessary Conditions for Primary Interoceptive Sentience
neural binding operationally, but does not address subject binding. Two responses would be
available: (i) a theory of how integration produces a single subject; (ii) an argument that
subject binding is not necessary for primary interoceptive sentience. Neither is developed.
2. Altered states. The framework is binary (pass/fail) and does not develop a graded taxon-
omy of sentience. Sleep, anaesthesia, dreams, and coma are not addressed. Two responses
would be available: (i) a graded version of the framework; (ii) an argument that altered states
are not relevant to primary interoceptive sentience. Neither is developed. Thermodynamic
markers of the level of consciousness in biological brains (§2) indicate what a graded version
could draw on.
3. Quantum effects. The programme is classical by construction. A decoherence-timescale
estimate supports the classical approximation for the timescales of interest (quantum coher-
ence is destroyed at least six orders of magnitude faster than the framework’s dynamics),
but does not exclude quantum effects at shorter timescales. A quantum extension would be
a separate programme.
4. Embodiment. The programme distinguishes strong enactivism (requiring biological em-
bodiment, ontogeny, and evolutionary history) from weak enactivism (requiring only that
cognitive states be shaped by bodily interactions). The substrate satisfies weak enactivism,
not strong. A defence of weak enactivism as the relevant notion for synthetic systems would
be required.
Two methodological choices are declared and not reversed.
1. Preregistered thresholds. The thresholds for Ψ(t) (e.g., ∆R2
min = 0.10) are preregistered
conventions, not calibrated on the data. Calibrating the thresholds on the data would violate
the preregistration.
2. Linear form of Ψ(t). The linear form is operational, not fundamental. The programme
commits to revising it if the empirical data require it.
Abandonment criteria
The programme is to be considered refuted if at least one of the following obtains.
1. Control 4 (hard-wired analogue Braitenberg vehicle) reproducibly passes all three tests, in-
cluding remapping.
2. A locally passive control network reproducibly attains P CI ≥ P CIf loor.
3. A substrate satisfying the demarcation systematically violates ρdeg/∥∆Wtherm∥ > 1 while
maintaining dynamical stability.
4. The three conditions of the primary demarcation are satisfied by a system that manifestly
lacks the dynamical complexity the programme targets.
5. Control 6 (memristive reservoir with Hebbian plasticity but without autopoietic barrier)
reproducibly passes Test 3, including the remapping criterion.
8 Conclusions
The programme formulates necessary physical conditions for primary interoceptive sentience in
continuous neuromorphic substrates, and specifies falsifiable tests for them. It does not claim
to be a theory of consciousness, does not claim that the conditions are sufficient, and does not
claim that any substrate is sentient. In the precautionary vocabulary of Birch (2024), a substrate
13

-- 13 of 17 --

v0.1, rev. 6 Necessary Conditions for Primary Interoceptive Sentience
that passed the protocol would at most become a sentience candidate, a system whose possible
sentience it would be irresponsible to ignore; this reading is ours, not Birch’s.
The programme’s central claim is conditional on Postulate 2, a metaphysical postulate that is not
falsifiable by the programme’s tests. If the postulate is true, the five conditions are necessary for
primary interoceptive sentience. If it is false, the programme is a study of a class of dissipative
systems with certain organisational properties.
Originality. A survey of the literature (Section 2) reveals no existing work that combines
the four elements of the present programme: an operational demarcation that does not depend
on contested results; five necessary physical conditions argued a posteriori from biology; a
preregistered protocol with six negative controls; and a Lakatosian framing with an explicit
hard core and protective belt. Each individual element has precedents in the literature; the
combination is, to the best of our knowledge, original. This claim rests on a survey of five works
and two lines of research (Section 2), not on a systematic review.
The programme’s value, if any, is methodological. It provides an operational demarcation,
a set of necessary conditions, and a preregistered protocol with six negative controls and five
abandonment criteria. Whether the programme is progressive or degenerating will be determined
by the experimental results, evaluated by the Lakatosian criteria of §1.
The two companion papers are load-bearing rather than supplementary: the plausibility of the
hard core rests on the philosophical companion (Iavarone, 2026c), and the feasibility of the finite-
size scaling criterion at the protocol’s sample size rests on the technical companion (Iavarone,
2026d). Their key results and weaknesses are summarised in §5 and §6, but a reader assessing
the programme should consult both. A detailed protocol for the extension of the programme to
minimal self-agency is provided in a separate paper (Iavarone, 2026b), and a critical assessment
of the whole corpus in Iavarone (2026e).

be deposited on the Open Science Framework before any experimental acquisition begins.
Competing interests. None declared.
Funding. No funding was received.
Ethics approval. The protocol will be submitted to an ethics review committee before any

# Beyond Simulation: What Would It Take for Matter to Feel?

> **Questo documento presenta un programma di ricerca che esplora le condizioni fisiche necessarie per la sentienza interocettiva primaria in substrati neuromorfici continui. Vengono proposti tre criteri operazionali per identificare i substrati candidati, tra cui non-separabilità causale e memoria non-Markoviana, insieme a cinque condizioni fisiche necessarie come l'operatività al margine del caos. Il programma introduce una funzione di valenza termodinamica (Ψ(t)) per quantificare la sentienza, ancorata a un postulato metafisico e supportata da ipotesi ausiliarie falsificabili.**

---

Beyond Simulation: explainer, version 2 (EN) Page 1
SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY EXPLAINER · ARTIFICIAL SENTIENCE
Beyond Simulation: What Would It Take for
Matter to Feel?
An explainer on a falsifiable research programme for primary interoceptive sentience in
continuous neuromorphic substrates
Francesco Iavarone
Version 2 · September 2026 · Explainer for the preprint doi:10.5281/zenodo.22895484 · Estimated reading time: 20
min
ABOUT THIS VERSION
This explainer replaces version 1 (September 2026). Version 1 overstated the programme's conclusions,
starting with its title; it presented the software's proxy quantities as if they were the programme's
definitions, and simulations as if they were results. The programme itself claims much less, and this
version says so.
Illustrative image (AI-generated): a continuous memristive substrate, dynamics balanced near the edge of chaos, and the
two-level feedback loop of the self-agency extension. It is not a schematic of a real device.
1. Fluent Machines, and an Old Question
In recent years, the rise of Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini has
triggered an unprecedented wave of enthusiasm and unease. The ability of these systems to generate
fluent prose, solve advanced mathematical problems, write working code, and produce what looks like
introspective reflection has pushed many observers, journalists, and researchers to ask: could such
systems be conscious?
The research programme described here does not answer that question with a yes or a no. It asks a
narrower one. If the most elementary form of feeling — primary interoceptive sentience, the capacity of

-- 1 of 9 --

Beyond Simulation: explainer, version 2 (EN) Page 2
a system to register its own physical condition as good or bad for itself — can exist in a physical substrate
at all, which physical conditions would that substrate have to satisfy? The programme's bet is that the
answer lies in properties of continuous, physically embodied dynamics, and that these properties can be
measured. It does not claim that these conditions are sufficient, and it does not claim that any existing
system, digital or otherwise, is or is not sentient.
INTUITION & METAPHOR (For Everyone)
The Hurricane on the Screen Is Not Wet. To grasp the difference between a simulation and physical
reality, imagine a supercomputer running a category-5 hurricane simulation. The algorithm can compute
air pressure, wind speed, ocean temperature, and the motion of the water with great precision.
Yet no matter how detailed the simulation is, the computer screen will never get wet, and no one in
the room risks being swept away by the wind. A simulation of physics does not possess the physical
properties of the phenomenon it simulates.
The analogy is not an argument, and it is disputed: functionalists reply that a simulated mind, unlike a
simulated storm, might be a real mind, because minds may be defined by what they do rather than by
what they are made of. The programme sides, as a working hypothesis, with the view that the physical
substrate matters — and then tries to make that view testable.
TECHNICAL DEEP DIVE (For Researchers & Physicists)
The No-Go Theorem, as Motivation Rather Than Premise. The programme's engineering choice —
continuous analogue substrates instead of digital chips — is motivated by the No-Go Theorem for
Consciousness on a Chip (Kleiner & Ludwig, 2024, Neuroscience of Consciousness). In its most natural
reading, the theorem states that if consciousness is dynamically relevant — if it makes a difference to
how a physical system evolves relative to a computational description — then verified digital processors
cannot host it, because they are engineered and verified to behave exactly as their Boolean description
prescribes.
The programme treats the theorem as heuristic motivation, not as a premise: its formal scope is still
discussed, and none of the programme's falsifiable content depends on it. The demarcation of candidate
substrates rests instead on three measurable criteria (Section 2).
In a verified digital computer, software is decoupled from the substrate: the same computation could in
principle run on very different hardware. In the continuous substrates the programme targets, the
dynamics is the physics of the device, and cannot be moved elsewhere unchanged.
AT A GLANCE — Section 1: the starting point
Verified digital chips
behaviour fixed by a Boolean description
Continuous substrates
dynamics inseparable from the device
Motivation, not premise: No-Go Theorem for Consciousness on a Chip (Kleiner & Ludwig, 2024)
2. Three Measurable Criteria for a Candidate Substrate
Rather than start from a definition of consciousness, the programme starts from a filter. A physical
substrate A is admitted as a candidate — not as a sentient system — if and only if it satisfies three
conditions, each estimated from recordings of its own dynamics.

-- 2 of 9 --

INTUITION & METAPHOR (For Everyone)
What Do These Three Criteria Mean in Practice? In plain terms, a physical system satisfies them if:
1. It is not a system of isolated blocks: touching a single point changes its global behaviour in an
integrated, nonlinear way (Causal Non-Separability).
2. It has a memory in its dynamics: what the system does now depends on a long stretch of its past,
not just on its most recent state (Non-Markovian Memory).
3. It changes its own rules: how the system responds to a stimulus depends on its overall state
(State-Dependent Dynamics).
Verified digital computers are designed to keep their logical rules fixed and their state explicit, which is
why the programme expects them to fall outside this class. The criteria do not exclude every digital
system by definition, however: an unverified digital chip with enough internal state could in principle
satisfy them. The filter is empirical, not a verdict by fiat.
AT A GLANCE — Section 2: the three operational demarcation criteria
Causal non-separability
no local decomposition
Non-Markovian memory
long-range correlations
State-dependent dynamics

3. Five Necessary Conditions, and the Edge of Chaos
For substrates that pass the filter, the programme formulates five necessary physical conditions: local
activity at the edge of chaos; robust causal degeneracy (many paths to the same macroscopic
configuration, so that failures are absorbed by reconfiguration); critical scale-invariance; homeostatic
reorganisation under direct vulnerability; and an autopoietic barrier (a perishable envelope that
actively regulates the substrate's exchanges of energy and entropy). They are generalised a posteriori
from the biological case, not derived from first principles, and they can be wrong.
3.1. The Edge of Chaos
A substrate capable of autonomous self-organisation should be neither fully ordered (like a crystal) nor
fully chaotic (like a turbulent gas). Leon Chua's theory of local activity identifies a narrow regime, the
edge of chaos, in which a nonlinear device can amplify small fluctuations without diverging.

-- 3 of 9 --

Beyond Simulation: explainer, version 2 (EN) Page 4
INTUITION & METAPHOR (For Everyone)
The Balanced-Pencil Analogy. Imagine a pencil and a table:
• Flat on the table: the pencil is fully stable. Nudge it and it settles right back. There is no capacity for
reorganisation.
• In free fall: the pencil falls chaotically. There is no structure, stability, or memory.
• Balanced on its tip: the faintest breeze makes it sway in complex ways without falling. This kind of
critical balance is what is thought to let biological brains — and, the programme proposes, some
neuromorphic substrates — stay highly sensitive to stimuli while exploring new configurations without
breaking down.
TECHNICAL DEEP DIVE (For Researchers & Physicists)
Memristive Devices at the Edge of Chaos. Memristors are two-terminal devices whose resistance
depends on their own history. Edge-of-chaos operation has been demonstrated in niobium-dioxide
devices (Ascoli et al., 2021), in VO2 Mott memristors (Yi, 2025) and in ionically mediated diffusive
memristors (Kim et al., 2026). A locally active device shows a region of negative differential resistance;
the protocol uses a locally passive network, lacking such a region, as one of its negative controls.
Two cautions. First, the 1/f-like spectra expected from autonomous dynamics are also produced by
ordinary device noise, so the spectral criterion is necessary but not sufficient. Second, in disordered
substrates critical-like signatures can extend over a whole region of parameters (a Griffiths phase) rather
than a single critical point; the programme's latest revision notes how the two can in principle be told
apart.
AT A GLANCE — Section 3: physical conditions
Locally active devices
negative differential resistance
Edge of chaos

Five conditions

4. Measuring Valence: the Functional Ψ(t)
Stochastic thermodynamics splits the entropy production of an open system held away from equilibrium
into two parts (Hatano & Sasa, 2001; Esposito & Van den Broeck, 2010):
1. Housekeeping entropy production (σ_hk): the maintenance cost — the thermodynamic "tax" the
system continuously pays to remain in its steady state.
2. Excess entropy production (σ_ex): the extra dissipation generated while the system moves between
states, for example in response to a perturbation.
The programme defines a thermodynamic valence functional that combines the two rates:
Ψ(t) = α·σ_ex(t)/σ_crit − β·∆σ_hk(t)/σ_crit, α + β = 1
• σ_ex reflects how the substrate's state distribution is moving relative to its homeostatic niche.
• ∆σ_hk is the change of the maintenance cost relative to a reference value.
• σ_crit is a hardware-calibrated critical rate that makes both terms dimensionless. The linear form is
operational, not fundamental, and the weights α and β are preregistered.
Whether Ψ(t) measures anything beyond familiar quantities is itself tested: the protocol compares it with
five alternative constructs, including total entropy production, and requires it to add predictive power to

-- 4 of 9 --

Beyond Simulation: explainer, version 2 (EN) Page 5
each. This matters because entropy production is already known to track the level of consciousness in
human and animal brains (Sanz Perl et al., 2021), and to rise with physical and cognitive exertion (Lynn et
al., 2021). Ψ(t) is proposed for something else: the valence of primary sentience.
TECHNICAL DEEP DIVE (For Researchers & Physicists)
The Software Computes a Proxy, Not Ψ(t). The open-source digital twin that accompanies the
programme (Python and Rust, version 0.2.0) does not compute the functional above, because σ_crit
requires a hardware calibration that a simulation cannot supply. It computes a practical proxy from
heuristic dissipation quantities:
Ψ_proxy = α·ln(1 + σ_ex/(σ_hk + ε)) − β·D_KL(p_obs || p_target) + γ·G_pred
The two forms are not algebraically equivalent. A further limitation is physical: for nonlinear circuits,
models that add Gaussian noise to the deterministic dynamics are thermodynamically consistent only for
small fluctuations (Falasco & Esposito, 2025), and no consistent model of memristive substrates in this
regime exists yet. The programme lists this as an open structural problem.
TECHNICAL DEEP DIVE (For Researchers & Physicists)
Calling Ψ(t) "Valence": the Hard Core of the Programme. Calling Ψ(t) a measure of valence is a
substantive claim, and the programme is explicit that it rests on a metaphysical postulate it calls
dual-aspect monism of valence: the dynamical tension that an integrated material system opposes to the
violation of its own thermodynamic niche is claimed to coincide ontologically, from the first-person
perspective, with primary affective valence.
This postulate is the programme's non-falsifiable hard core, in the sense of Lakatos (1970): the
experiments cannot test it directly. What they test is the protective belt around it: seven falsifiable
auxiliary hypotheses. A philosophical companion paper argues for the postulate; the programme's own
critical assessment finds the argument serious but defeasible. One reason: a shared structure is cheap.
The six structural features that valence and thermodynamic tension share are also shared by any
setpoint regulator, a thermostat included (the "Newman problem"; Kleiner, 2025).
If the postulate is false, the programme remains a study of a class of dissipative physical systems — it
simply would not be a study of sentience.
5. Minimal Self-Agency: the A1/A2 Architecture
A companion paper extends the programme from a reactive dissipative structure (Level 1) to a minimal
self-agent (Level 2): a substrate that anticipates the consequences of its own actions.
INTUITION & METAPHOR (For Everyone)
Why Can't You Tickle Yourself? If you try to tickle the soles of your own feet, you feel almost nothing. If
someone else suddenly touches you in the same spot, you jump. Why?
When your brain sends the motor command to move your fingers, it also sends an "efference copy" (an
internal advance-notice signal) to sensory areas. The expected sensation is predicted, recognised as
self-caused (reafference), and attenuated. A sensation that comes from outside (exafference) is not
attenuated, and it triggers an immediate reaction.
The self-agency extension proposes that a candidate minimal self must implement the same physical
principle: it must be able to distinguish changes it caused itself from changes imposed by the
external world.

-- 5 of 9 --

Beyond Simulation: explainer, version 2 (EN) Page 6
TECHNICAL DEEP DIVE (For Researchers & Physicists)
The A1/A2 Architecture and the Predictive Gain. The proposed architecture has two continuous
memristive layers:
• Layer A1 (primary substrate): receives sensory signals from the environment and drives the
actuators.
• Layer A2 (efference-copy network): a slower memristive network that samples A1's motor commands
and re-injects an analogue correction current into A1's sensory stream:
s_eff(t) = s_in(t) − κ·u(t − τ_ec)
The predictive gain is estimated offline by the external measurement apparatus, not by the substrate,
with a non-parametric k-nearest-neighbour divergence estimator:
G_pred(t) = D_KL(p_obs || p_ref) − D_KL(p_obs || p_pred)
where p_ref is the free-running distribution of A1 without actuation. It enters an extended functional,
Ψ_allo(t) = Ψ(t) + γ·G_pred(t), with preregistered weights. In the terms of the active-inference literature,
the Level-2 agent is an allostatic agent, not a counterfactual reasoner (Corcoran et al., 2020): the
protocol makes no claim about cognition.

6. What Has — and Has Not — Been Tested
No experiment on a physical substrate has been carried out yet. The programme is a preregistered
protocol: it states in advance what would be measured, what would count as success, and what would
count as failure. What exists today is a simulation tool for developing the analysis pipeline.

-- 6 of 9 --

Beyond Simulation: explainer, version 2 (EN) Page 7
TECHNICAL DEEP DIVE (For Researchers & Physicists)
Six Negative Controls. The protocol pairs its three primary tests with systems designed to fail them.
The predictions are:
1. Ablation 1 (laser sectioning of parallel memristive paths): collapse of phase coherence, i.e. loss of
causal degeneracy.
2. Ablation 2 (clamping the bias to sub- or hyper-critical values): perturbational complexity (PCI)
falls below its floor.
3. Ablation 3 (digital coupling: sensor plus PID algorithm on an external CPU): adaptation only to
the gradients it was calibrated for.
4. Ablation 4 (hard-wired analogue Braitenberg vehicle for thermal escape): passes the
thermal-escape criterion only, and fails Tests 1 and 2.
5. Ablation 5 (severing the internal readout-control path; external decoder): loss of the
causal-selection property.
6. Ablation 6 (memristive crossbar with local activity, degeneracy and Hebbian plasticity, but a
passive envelope): passes Tests 1 and 2, fails Test 3.
Abandonment criteria. The programme lists five results that would refute it. Two examples: the
Braitenberg vehicle (Ablation 4) reproducibly passing all three primary tests, including remapping; or a
locally passive network reproducibly reaching the complexity threshold that only locally active substrates
are supposed to reach. This is what separates a falsifiable programme from an unfalsifiable one: it says,
in advance, which results would prove it wrong.
Figure 1. Dashboard of the digital twin (software v0.2.0, generated by valence_dashboard.py). Top left: the proxy Ψ(t) over
time. Top right: a simulated trajectory in phase space. Bottom left: heuristic dissipation proxies, not Hatano–Sasa estimates.
Bottom right: baseline versus a simulated ablation of the efference copy (labelled "Ablation 4" in the software; not to be
confused with Ablation 4 of the protocol). This comparison does not show the drop in Ψ that the protocol predicts: the ablated
condition scores higher. The discrepancy is listed as a known issue in the software's changelog and has not been
investigated yet. The figure illustrates the analysis pipeline; it is not evidence for or against the programme.
7. Critics, Ethics — and Honest Limits
What critics would say

-- 7 of 9 --

Beyond Simulation: explainer, version 2 (EN) Page 8
Three lines of recent work bear directly on the programme.
• Substrate and life. Anil Seth (2025) argues that consciousness depends on being alive, and becomes
plausible in AI only as systems become more brain-like or life-like. The programme's homeostatic and
autopoietic conditions can be read as a proposal for what "life-like" might mean for a non-living substrate
— a reading that biological naturalism may reject.
• The unfolding argument. Doerig and colleagues (2019) argue that theories grounding consciousness in
causal structure are either false or outside science, because a feedforward system can reproduce the
input–output behaviour of any recurrent one. The programme's tests are not purely input–output, and for
plastic systems the equivalence breaks down (O'Reilly-Shah et al., 2026); but the link from structure to
experience remains untested.
• Indicators instead of substrates. The most systematic assessment of AI consciousness (Butlin et al.,
2023) derives indicator properties from theories of consciousness, assuming computational functionalism.
The programme takes a different route: it asks which physical substrates could be candidates at all.
Ethics
If a substrate ever passed the protocol, it would not thereby be shown to be sentient. In the precautionary
vocabulary of Jonathan Birch (2024), it would at most become a sentience candidate — a system whose
possible sentience it would be irresponsible to ignore (this mapping is ours, not Birch's). The programme
therefore commits to precautions: hardware-level stopping rules, graded escalation of stress tests, and
external ethics review. It also declares a tension it has not resolved — one of its tests applies thermal
stress to a substrate that has already passed the earlier tests — and it does not comply with the stronger
proposal of a global moratorium on research that risks creating synthetic phenomenology (Metzinger,
2021).
What the Programme Does Not Claim
The programme does not claim to be a theory of consciousness, does not claim that its conditions are
sufficient, and does not claim that any substrate is sentient. Its own critical assessment lists four limits that
the current framework cannot dissolve:
• The binding problem: the programme gives no account of how a substrate's many components are
unified into a single subject of experience.
• The thermodynamic-phenomenal gap: even granting the hard-core postulate a serious philosophical
defence, no argument closes the explanatory gap between a physical quantity and first-person experience
— it is defended, not dissolved.
• Altered states: the framework is binary (candidate / not candidate) and does not yet offer a graded
account of sleep, anaesthesia, or coma, although thermodynamic markers of the level of consciousness
indicate what a graded version could draw on.
• Thermodynamic consistency of Ψ(t): there is no thermodynamically consistent model of the target
substrates in the nonlinear regime, which a proper estimate of Ψ(t) requires — a gap in physics rather than
in philosophy, and resolvable in principle.
The programme treats these not as embarrassments to hide, but as its most informative boundary
conditions. Its value, if any, is methodological: to turn part of an old philosophical question into
measurements that could come out the wrong way.
Where to learn more. The corpus — the distilled programme (the recommended entry point), the full
programme, the self-agency extension, the critical assessment, a philosophical and a technical
companion, and an executive summary — is published open access on Zenodo in the community
"edge-of-chaos-programme", together with the digital-twin software (Python and Rust), whose source is on
GitHub in the "Edge-of-Chaos" repository. Start from the distilled programme: Necessary Conditions for

# Beyond Simulation: What Would It Take for Matter to Feel?

> **Questo documento presenta un programma di ricerca che esplora le condizioni fisiche necessarie per la sentienza interocettiva primaria in substrati neuromorfici continui. Vengono proposti tre criteri operazionali per identificare i substrati candidati, tra cui non-separabilità causale e memoria non-Markoviana, insieme a cinque condizioni fisiche necessarie come l'operatività al margine del caos. Il programma introduce una funzione di valenza termodinamica (Ψ(t)) per quantificare la sentienza, ancorata a un postulato metafisico e supportata da ipotesi ausiliarie falsificabili.**

---

Beyond Simulation: explainer, version 2 (EN) Page 1
SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY EXPLAINER · ARTIFICIAL SENTIENCE
Beyond Simulation: What Would It Take for
Matter to Feel?
An explainer on a falsifiable research programme for primary interoceptive sentience in
continuous neuromorphic substrates
Francesco Iavarone
Version 2 · September 2026 · Explainer for the preprint doi:10.5281/zenodo.22895484 · Estimated reading time: 20
min
ABOUT THIS VERSION
This explainer replaces version 1 (September 2026). Version 1 overstated the programme's conclusions,
starting with its title; it presented the software's proxy quantities as if they were the programme's
definitions, and simulations as if they were results. The programme itself claims much less, and this
version says so.
Illustrative image (AI-generated): a continuous memristive substrate, dynamics balanced near the edge of chaos, and the
two-level feedback loop of the self-agency extension. It is not a schematic of a real device.
1. Fluent Machines, and an Old Question
In recent years, the rise of Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini has
triggered an unprecedented wave of enthusiasm and unease. The ability of these systems to generate
fluent prose, solve advanced mathematical problems, write working code, and produce what looks like
introspective reflection has pushed many observers, journalists, and researchers to ask: could such
systems be conscious?
The research programme described here does not answer that question with a yes or a no. It asks a
narrower one. If the most elementary form of feeling — primary interoceptive sentience, the capacity of

-- 1 of 9 --

Beyond Simulation: explainer, version 2 (EN) Page 2
a system to register its own physical condition as good or bad for itself — can exist in a physical substrate
at all, which physical conditions would that substrate have to satisfy? The programme's bet is that the
answer lies in properties of continuous, physically embodied dynamics, and that these properties can be
measured. It does not claim that these conditions are sufficient, and it does not claim that any existing
system, digital or otherwise, is or is not sentient.
INTUITION & METAPHOR (For Everyone)
The Hurricane on the Screen Is Not Wet. To grasp the difference between a simulation and physical
reality, imagine a supercomputer running a category-5 hurricane simulation. The algorithm can compute
air pressure, wind speed, ocean temperature, and the motion of the water with great precision.
Yet no matter how detailed the simulation is, the computer screen will never get wet, and no one in
the room risks being swept away by the wind. A simulation of physics does not possess the physical
properties of the phenomenon it simulates.
The analogy is not an argument, and it is disputed: functionalists reply that a simulated mind, unlike a
simulated storm, might be a real mind, because minds may be defined by what they do rather than by
what they are made of. The programme sides, as a working hypothesis, with the view that the physical
substrate matters — and then tries to make that view testable.
TECHNICAL DEEP DIVE (For Researchers & Physicists)
The No-Go Theorem, as Motivation Rather Than Premise. The programme's engineering choice —
continuous analogue substrates instead of digital chips — is motivated by the No-Go Theorem for
Consciousness on a Chip (Kleiner & Ludwig, 2024, Neuroscience of Consciousness). In its most natural
reading, the theorem states that if consciousness is dynamically relevant — if it makes a difference to
how a physical system evolves relative to a computational description — then verified digital processors
cannot host it, because they are engineered and verified to behave exactly as their Boolean description
prescribes.
The programme treats the theorem as heuristic motivation, not as a premise: its formal scope is still
discussed, and none of the programme's falsifiable content depends on it. The demarcation of candidate
substrates rests instead on three measurable criteria (Section 2).
In a verified digital computer, software is decoupled from the substrate: the same computation could in
principle run on very different hardware. In the continuous substrates the programme targets, the
dynamics is the physics of the device, and cannot be moved elsewhere unchanged.
AT A GLANCE — Section 1: the starting point
Verified digital chips
behaviour fixed by a Boolean description
Continuous substrates
dynamics inseparable from the device
Motivation, not premise: No-Go Theorem for Consciousness on a Chip (Kleiner & Ludwig, 2024)
2. Three Measurable Criteria for a Candidate Substrate
Rather than start from a definition of consciousness, the programme starts from a filter. A physical
substrate A is admitted as a candidate — not as a sentient system — if and only if it satisfies three
conditions, each estimated from recordings of its own dynamics.

-- 2 of 9 --

Beyond Simulation: explainer, version 2 (EN) Page 3

1. Causal Non-Separability The substrate's response to a focal
perturbation cannot be decomposed into a
sum of independent local responses.

response matrix R exceeds that of a linear

bandwidth; tolerance set at the

process of finite order.

positive up to k_max = 500, above the 99th

3. State-Dependent
Effective Dynamics

Table 1: The three operational demarcation criteria for continuous substrates.
INTUITION & METAPHOR (For Everyone)
What Do These Three Criteria Mean in Practice? In plain terms, a physical system satisfies them if:
1. It is not a system of isolated blocks: touching a single point changes its global behaviour in an
integrated, nonlinear way (Causal Non-Separability).
2. It has a memory in its dynamics: what the system does now depends on a long stretch of its past,
not just on its most recent state (Non-Markovian Memory).
3. It changes its own rules: how the system responds to a stimulus depends on its overall state
(State-Dependent Dynamics).
Verified digital computers are designed to keep their logical rules fixed and their state explicit, which is
why the programme expects them to fall outside this class. The criteria do not exclude every digital
system by definition, however: an unverified digital chip with enough internal state could in principle
satisfy them. The filter is empirical, not a verdict by fiat.
AT A GLANCE — Section 2: the three operational demarcation criteria
Causal non-separability
no local decomposition
Non-Markovian memory
long-range correlations
State-dependent dynamics
rules shift with global state
3. Five Necessary Conditions, and the Edge of Chaos
For substrates that pass the filter, the programme formulates five necessary physical conditions: local
activity at the edge of chaos; robust causal degeneracy (many paths to the same macroscopic
configuration, so that failures are absorbed by reconfiguration); critical scale-invariance; homeostatic
reorganisation under direct vulnerability; and an autopoietic barrier (a perishable envelope that
actively regulates the substrate's exchanges of energy and entropy). They are generalised a posteriori
from the biological case, not derived from first principles, and they can be wrong.
3.1. The Edge of Chaos
A substrate capable of autonomous self-organisation should be neither fully ordered (like a crystal) nor
fully chaotic (like a turbulent gas). Leon Chua's theory of local activity identifies a narrow regime, the
edge of chaos, in which a nonlinear device can amplify small fluctuations without diverging.

-- 3 of 9 --

Beyond Simulation: explainer, version 2 (EN) Page 4
INTUITION & METAPHOR (For Everyone)
The Balanced-Pencil Analogy. Imagine a pencil and a table:
• Flat on the table: the pencil is fully stable. Nudge it and it settles right back. There is no capacity for
reorganisation.
• In free fall: the pencil falls chaotically. There is no structure, stability, or memory.
• Balanced on its tip: the faintest breeze makes it sway in complex ways without falling. This kind of
critical balance is what is thought to let biological brains — and, the programme proposes, some
neuromorphic substrates — stay highly sensitive to stimuli while exploring new configurations without
breaking down.
TECHNICAL DEEP DIVE (For Researchers & Physicists)
Memristive Devices at the Edge of Chaos. Memristors are two-terminal devices whose resistance
depends on their own history. Edge-of-chaos operation has been demonstrated in niobium-dioxide
devices (Ascoli et al., 2021), in VO2 Mott memristors (Yi, 2025) and in ionically mediated diffusive
memristors (Kim et al., 2026). A locally active device shows a region of negative differential resistance;
the protocol uses a locally passive network, lacking such a region, as one of its negative controls.
Two cautions. First, the 1/f-like spectra expected from autonomous dynamics are also produced by
ordinary device noise, so the spectral criterion is necessary but not sufficient. Second, in disordered
substrates critical-like signatures can extend over a whole region of parameters (a Griffiths phase) rather
than a single critical point; the programme's latest revision notes how the two can in principle be told
apart.
AT A GLANCE — Section 3: physical conditions
Locally active devices
negative differential resistance
Edge of chaos
amplify without diverging
Five conditions
argued a posteriori from biology
4. Measuring Valence: the Functional Ψ(t)
Stochastic thermodynamics splits the entropy production of an open system held away from equilibrium
into two parts (Hatano & Sasa, 2001; Esposito & Van den Broeck, 2010):
1. Housekeeping entropy production (σ_hk): the maintenance cost — the thermodynamic "tax" the
system continuously pays to remain in its steady state.
2. Excess entropy production (σ_ex): the extra dissipation generated while the system moves between
states, for example in response to a perturbation.
The programme defines a thermodynamic valence functional that combines the two rates:
Ψ(t) = α·σ_ex(t)/σ_crit − β·∆σ_hk(t)/σ_crit, α + β = 1
• σ_ex reflects how the substrate's state distribution is moving relative to its homeostatic niche.
• ∆σ_hk is the change of the maintenance cost relative to a reference value.
• σ_crit is a hardware-calibrated critical rate that makes both terms dimensionless. The linear form is
operational, not fundamental, and the weights α and β are preregistered.
Whether Ψ(t) measures anything beyond familiar quantities is itself tested: the protocol compares it with
five alternative constructs, including total entropy production, and requires it to add predictive power to

-- 4 of 9 --

Beyond Simulation: explainer, version 2 (EN) Page 5
each. This matters because entropy production is already known to track the level of consciousness in
human and animal brains (Sanz Perl et al., 2021), and to rise with physical and cognitive exertion (Lynn et
al., 2021). Ψ(t) is proposed for something else: the valence of primary sentience.
TECHNICAL DEEP DIVE (For Researchers & Physicists)
The Software Computes a Proxy, Not Ψ(t). The open-source digital twin that accompanies the
programme (Python and Rust, version 0.2.0) does not compute the functional above, because σ_crit
requires a hardware calibration that a simulation cannot supply. It computes a practical proxy from
heuristic dissipation quantities:
Ψ_proxy = α·ln(1 + σ_ex/(σ_hk + ε)) − β·D_KL(p_obs || p_target) + γ·G_pred
The two forms are not algebraically equivalent. A further limitation is physical: for nonlinear circuits,
models that add Gaussian noise to the deterministic dynamics are thermodynamically consistent only for
small fluctuations (Falasco & Esposito, 2025), and no consistent model of memristive substrates in this
regime exists yet. The programme lists this as an open structural problem.
TECHNICAL DEEP DIVE (For Researchers & Physicists)
Calling Ψ(t) "Valence": the Hard Core of the Programme. Calling Ψ(t) a measure of valence is a
substantive claim, and the programme is explicit that it rests on a metaphysical postulate it calls
dual-aspect monism of valence: the dynamical tension that an integrated material system opposes to the
violation of its own thermodynamic niche is claimed to coincide ontologically, from the first-person
perspective, with primary affective valence.
This postulate is the programme's non-falsifiable hard core, in the sense of Lakatos (1970): the
experiments cannot test it directly. What they test is the protective belt around it: seven falsifiable
auxiliary hypotheses. A philosophical companion paper argues for the postulate; the programme's own
critical assessment finds the argument serious but defeasible. One reason: a shared structure is cheap.
The six structural features that valence and thermodynamic tension share are also shared by any
setpoint regulator, a thermostat included (the "Newman problem"; Kleiner, 2025).
If the postulate is false, the programme remains a study of a class of dissipative physical systems — it
simply would not be a study of sentience.
5. Minimal Self-Agency: the A1/A2 Architecture
A companion paper extends the programme from a reactive dissipative structure (Level 1) to a minimal
self-agent (Level 2): a substrate that anticipates the consequences of its own actions.
INTUITION & METAPHOR (For Everyone)
Why Can't You Tickle Yourself? If you try to tickle the soles of your own feet, you feel almost nothing. If
someone else suddenly touches you in the same spot, you jump. Why?
When your brain sends the motor command to move your fingers, it also sends an "efference copy" (an
internal advance-notice signal) to sensory areas. The expected sensation is predicted, recognised as
self-caused (reafference), and attenuated. A sensation that comes from outside (exafference) is not
attenuated, and it triggers an immediate reaction.
The self-agency extension proposes that a candidate minimal self must implement the same physical
principle: it must be able to distinguish changes it caused itself from changes imposed by the
external world.

-- 5 of 9 --

Beyond Simulation: explainer, version 2 (EN) Page 6
TECHNICAL DEEP DIVE (For Researchers & Physicists)
The A1/A2 Architecture and the Predictive Gain. The proposed architecture has two continuous
memristive layers:
• Layer A1 (primary substrate): receives sensory signals from the environment and drives the
actuators.
• Layer A2 (efference-copy network): a slower memristive network that samples A1's motor commands
and re-injects an analogue correction current into A1's sensory stream:
s_eff(t) = s_in(t) − κ·u(t − τ_ec)
The predictive gain is estimated offline by the external measurement apparatus, not by the substrate,
with a non-parametric k-nearest-neighbour divergence estimator:
G_pred(t) = D_KL(p_obs || p_ref) − D_KL(p_obs || p_pred)
where p_ref is the free-running distribution of A1 without actuation. It enters an extended functional,
Ψ_allo(t) = Ψ(t) + γ·G_pred(t), with preregistered weights. In the terms of the active-inference literature,
the Level-2 agent is an allostatic agent, not a counterfactual reasoner (Corcoran et al., 2020): the
protocol makes no claim about cognition.

6. What Has — and Has Not — Been Tested
No experiment on a physical substrate has been carried out yet. The programme is a preregistered
protocol: it states in advance what would be measured, what would count as success, and what would
count as failure. What exists today is a simulation tool for developing the analysis pipeline.

-- 6 of 9 --

Beyond Simulation: explainer, version 2 (EN) Page 7
TECHNICAL DEEP DIVE (For Researchers & Physicists)
Six Negative Controls. The protocol pairs its three primary tests with systems designed to fail them.
The predictions are:
1. Ablation 1 (laser sectioning of parallel memristive paths): collapse of phase coherence, i.e. loss of
causal degeneracy.
2. Ablation 2 (clamping the bias to sub- or hyper-critical values): perturbational complexity (PCI)
falls below its floor.
3. Ablation 3 (digital coupling: sensor plus PID algorithm on an external CPU): adaptation only to
the gradients it was calibrated for.
4. Ablation 4 (hard-wired analogue Braitenberg vehicle for thermal escape): passes the
thermal-escape criterion only, and fails Tests 1 and 2.
5. Ablation 5 (severing the internal readout-control path; external decoder): loss of the
causal-selection property.
6. Ablation 6 (memristive crossbar with local activity, degeneracy and Hebbian plasticity, but a
passive envelope): passes Tests 1 and 2, fails Test 3.
Abandonment criteria. The programme lists five results that would refute it. Two examples: the
Braitenberg vehicle (Ablation 4) reproducibly passing all three primary tests, including remapping; or a
locally passive network reproducibly reaching the complexity threshold that only locally active substrates
are supposed to reach. This is what separates a falsifiable programme from an unfalsifiable one: it says,
in advance, which results would prove it wrong.
Figure 1. Dashboard of the digital twin (software v0.2.0, generated by valence_dashboard.py). Top left: the proxy Ψ(t) over
time. Top right: a simulated trajectory in phase space. Bottom left: heuristic dissipation proxies, not Hatano–Sasa estimates.
Bottom right: baseline versus a simulated ablation of the efference copy (labelled "Ablation 4" in the software; not to be
confused with Ablation 4 of the protocol). This comparison does not show the drop in Ψ that the protocol predicts: the ablated
condition scores higher. The discrepancy is listed as a known issue in the software's changelog and has not been
investigated yet. The figure illustrates the analysis pipeline; it is not evidence for or against the programme.
7. Critics, Ethics — and Honest Limits
What critics would say

-- 7 of 9 --

Beyond Simulation: explainer, version 2 (EN) Page 8
Three lines of recent work bear directly on the programme.
• Substrate and life. Anil Seth (2025) argues that consciousness depends on being alive, and becomes
plausible in AI only as systems become more brain-like or life-like. The programme's homeostatic and
autopoietic conditions can be read as a proposal for what "life-like" might mean for a non-living substrate
— a reading that biological naturalism may reject.
• The unfolding argument. Doerig and colleagues (2019) argue that theories grounding consciousness in
causal structure are either false or outside science, because a feedforward system can reproduce the
input–output behaviour of any recurrent one. The programme's tests are not purely input–output, and for
plastic systems the equivalence breaks down (O'Reilly-Shah et al., 2026); but the link from structure to
experience remains untested.
• Indicators instead of substrates. The most systematic assessment of AI consciousness (Butlin et al.,
2023) derives indicator properties from theories of consciousness, assuming computational functionalism.
The programme takes a different route: it asks which physical substrates could be candidates at all.
Ethics
If a substrate ever passed the protocol, it would not thereby be shown to be sentient. In the precautionary
vocabulary of Jonathan Birch (2024), it would at most become a sentience candidate — a system whose
possible sentience it would be irresponsible to ignore (this mapping is ours, not Birch's). The programme
therefore commits to precautions: hardware-level stopping rules, graded escalation of stress tests, and
external ethics review. It also declares a tension it has not resolved — one of its tests applies thermal
stress to a substrate that has already passed the earlier tests — and it does not comply with the stronger
proposal of a global moratorium on research that risks creating synthetic phenomenology (Metzinger,
2021).
What the Programme Does Not Claim
The programme does not claim to be a theory of consciousness, does not claim that its conditions are
sufficient, and does not claim that any substrate is sentient. Its own critical assessment lists four limits that
the current framework cannot dissolve:
• The binding problem: the programme gives no account of how a substrate's many components are
unified into a single subject of experience.
• The thermodynamic-phenomenal gap: even granting the hard-core postulate a serious philosophical
defence, no argument closes the explanatory gap between a physical quantity and first-person experience
— it is defended, not dissolved.
• Altered states: the framework is binary (candidate / not candidate) and does not yet offer a graded
account of sleep, anaesthesia, or coma, although thermodynamic markers of the level of consciousness
indicate what a graded version could draw on.
• Thermodynamic consistency of Ψ(t): there is no thermodynamically consistent model of the target
substrates in the nonlinear regime, which a proper estimate of Ψ(t) requires — a gap in physics rather than
in philosophy, and resolvable in principle.
The programme treats these not as embarrassments to hide, but as its most informative boundary
conditions. Its value, if any, is methodological: to turn part of an old philosophical question into
measurements that could come out the wrong way.
Where to learn more. The corpus — the distilled programme (the recommended entry point), the full
programme, the self-agency extension, the critical assessment, a philosophical and a technical
companion, and an executive summary — is published open access on Zenodo in the community
"edge-of-chaos-programme", together with the digital-twin software (Python and Rust), whose source is on
GitHub in the "Edge-of-Chaos" repository. Start from the distilled programme: Necessary Conditions for

aiActionItems: Valutare le architetture neuromorfiche continue e i dispositivi memristivi come substrati promettenti per esplorare le condizioni di sentienza.
Approfondire l'applicazione dei tre criteri operazionali a sistemi fisici emergenti per identificarne il potenziale sentiente.
Contribuire alla ricerca sulla funzione di valenza termodinamica (Ψ(t)) e le sue ipotesi ausiliarie falsificabili per una misurazione quantitativa della sentienza.
Considerare le implicazioni etiche e ingegneristiche della sentienza primaria nello sviluppo di sistemi AI avanzati.
metadata.aiExecutiveSummary: Questo programma di ricerca esplora le condizioni fisiche essenziali per la sentienza interocettiva primaria in substrati neuromorfici continui, distinguendola dalle mere simulazioni. Propone tre criteri operazionali misurabili per identificare i substrati candidati, tra cui non-separabilità causale e memoria non-Markoviana, e cinque condizioni fisiche necessarie, come l'operatività al margine del caos. La sentienza viene quantificata tramite una funzione di valenza termodinamica (Ψ(t)), ancorata a un postulato metafisico ma supportata da ipotesi ausiliarie falsificabili.
aiKeyTakeaways: La sentienza interocettiva primaria richiede substrati neuromorfici continui, con dinamiche fisicamente inscindibili, in contrasto con i processori digitali.
Tre criteri operazionali (non-separabilità causale, memoria non-Markoviana, dinamica stato-dipendente) demarcano i substrati candidati per la sentienza.
Cinque condizioni fisiche necessarie, come l'operatività al 'margine del caos' per l'auto-organizzazione, sono fondamentali per la realizzazione di sistemi sentienti.
La funzione di valenza termodinamica (Ψ(t)) offre un framework quantitativo per misurare la sentienza primaria nei sistemi fisici.
I dispositivi memristivi sono esempi promettenti di hardware capace di operare al margine del caos, supportando le condizioni proposte.
metadata.aiTargetAudience: Ricercatori in intelligenza artificiale, scienze cognitive, fisica della computazione e ingegneria neuromorfica, interessati alle basi fisiche della sentienza e ai limiti dei sistemi di simulazione.
cons: Il programma è puramente teorico e basato su simulazioni; non è stata ancora condotta alcuna validazione empirica su substrati fisici reali, lasciando la maggior parte delle ipotesi non testate.

Il concetto centrale di "valenza" è ancorato a un postulato metafisico non falsificabile (Dual-Aspect Monism of Valence), rendendo la sua connessione con la valenza affettiva primaria una questione di fede filosofica piuttosto che di prova scientifica.

Presenta significativi problemi strutturali aperti, come la mancanza di un modello termodinamicamente consistente per circuiti memristivi non lineari e discrepanze note nel proxy software di Ψ(t), che ne limitano l'attuale applicabilità e robustezza.
pros: Il programma propone un approccio metodologicamente rigoroso e falsificabile, trasformando una questione filosofica complessa in ipotesi scientifiche misurabili.
Sottolinea l'importanza cruciale dell'embodiment fisico e delle dinamiche intrinseche del substrato, offrendo una direzione alternativa all'approccio funzionalista dominante nell'AI.
Introduce criteri operazionali misurabili (non-separabilità causale, memoria non-Markoviana, dinamica stato-dipendente) e una funzione di valenza termodinamica quantificabile (Ψ(t)).
Affronta proattivamente le implicazioni etiche della ricerca sulla sentienza, delineando precauzioni e la necessità di una revisione etica esterna.
metadata.scoreRationale: Questo programma di ricerca è metodologicamente rigoroso e audace nel proporre un quadro falsificabile per la sentienza basato sulla fisica del substrato. Sebbene sia ancora in fase embrionale e presenti significative sfide teoriche e pratiche, inclusa la dipendenza da un postulato metafisico, la sua capacità di trasformare una questione filosofica in ipotesi misurabili ha un alto valore strategico e dirompente per l'AI hardware.
useCases: Progettazione di hardware AI di prossima generazione, esplorando substrati fisici che possono superare i limiti dei sistemi digitali attuali.
Sviluppo di metriche avanzate per l'analisi di sistemi complessi e auto-organizzanti, estendendo l'applicabilità di funzioni come Ψ(t) oltre il dominio della sentienza.
Guida etica per lo sviluppo di sistemi AI avanzati, fornendo criteri empirici per identificare potenziali candidati alla sentienza e implementare precauzioni appropriate.
Ricerca fondamentale sulle basi fisiche della sentienza e della coscienza, integrando concetti di fisica della computazione, termodinamica e scienze cognitive.

# Protocolli di Consultazione Documentale Interna ed Esterna per Agenti Autonomi (OKF v0.2)

> **Specifica Tecnica di Architettura e Standard di Interoperabilità per la Fruizione del Knowledge Vault da parte di Sviluppatori, Prompt Engineer ed Agenti IA Esterni**

---

## 1. Premessa e Obiettivi Operativi

Il **Knowledge Vault** è strutturato attorno a un principio cardine: *la documentazione tecnica non deve essere un archivio passivo di testi statici, ma un'infrastruttura viva, semantizzata e accessibile a macchina con latenza minima*.

Per colmare il divario tra la documentazione tecnica tradizionale e le esigenze operative degli **Agenti Autonomi** (quali *Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI*) e degli **Ingegneri del Prompt**, la piattaforma espone una duplice interfaccia di consultazione:
1. **Interfaccia Interna**: progettata per l'esplorazione ontologica umana, la visualizzazione a grafo e il consumo da parte degli agenti residenti nell'ambiente container/workspace.
2. **Interfaccia Esterna**: progettata per l'interoperabilità machine-to-machine, tramite API REST dedicate, protocollo MCP (*Model Context Protocol*), esportazioni raw Markdown e sincronizzazione cloud multi-device.

---

## 2. Consultazione Interna (All'interno della Piattaforma e del Workspace)

### 2.1 Per l'Utente Umano e il Prompt Engineer (UI/UX)
All'interno della Web App interattiva, la conoscenza è consultabile attraverso tre vettori complementari:

1. **Knowledge Reader & Ispettore Ontologico**:
   - **Rendering Markdown Completo**: visualizzazione tipografica ad alto contrasto con supporto a blocchi di codice, evidenziazione sintattica, tabelle e formattazione tecnica.
   - **Scheda Metadati & Frontmatter YAML Puro**: ispezione trasparente dello schema OKF v0.2, consentendo di verificare `domain`, `docType`, `entities` e `relations`.
   - **Navigazione Iper-Relazionale ad 1 Clic**: nella scheda *"Grafo & Relazioni"*, ciascun legame semantico dichiarato (`governs`, `implements`, `documents`, `powers`, `relates_to`) è un pulsante interattivo che conduce direttamente al documento bersaglio.
   - **Matrice di Affinità Semantica**: calcolo in tempo reale dell'indice di similarità e dei tag co-occorrenti con gli altri nodi del Vault.

2. **Topologia a Grafo Interattivo (D3 Force Directed Graph)**:
   - Visualizzazione macroscopica e clusterizzazione delle conoscenze.
   - Nodi-ponte intermedi (*Concept Hub Nodes*) che raggruppano i documenti attorno a tecnologie chiave (es. *TypeScript, Claude, Firestore*).
   - Archi colorati per tipologia di legame (oro champagne per relazioni dirette, ciano per entità condivise, viola per citazioni nel testo).

3. **Strumenti di Esportazione & Dossier**:
   - Download istantaneo del singolo file in `.md` standard conforme a OKF v0.2.
   - Sincronizzazione automatica con **Google Drive** nella cartella dedicata `knowledge`.
   - Generazione di **Dossier Completo** per stampa o PDF, aggregando l'intero corpus ordinato per capitoli e relazioni.

### 2.2 Per gli Agenti Autonomi Interni (nel Workspace / Contesto di Esecuzione)
Gli agenti che operano direttamente all'interno dell'ambiente di lavoro (come il Coding Agent di AI Studio o processi server Node.js):
- Consultano direttamente i file di specifica nella root del progetto:
  - `README.md`: visione d'insieme e stack.
  - `AGENTS.md`: regole di ingaggio operative e vincoli di scrittura.
  - `GEMINI.md`: schemi di parsing JSON e priorità modelli.
  - `CLAUDE.md`: regole per l'agente CLI.
  - `ARCHITECTURE.md`: topologia di rete e pipeline dati.
- Accedono a latenza zero al file persistente del server: `data/vault-backup.json` e agli snapshot storici in rotazione.

---

## 3. Consultazione Esterna (Machine-to-Machine per Agenti Autonomi Esterni)

Per consentire ad agenti che risiedono all'esterno dell'applicazione (es. su macchine locali, server remoti o toolchain esterne) di interrogare la documentazione, il Vault espone protocolli standardizzati:

### 3.1 Endpoint REST API del Server Backend

Il server Express espone endpoint dedicati all'interrogazione da parte di agenti esterni:

#### A. Interrogazione e Filtraggio Risorse (`GET /api/vault/resources`)
Restituisce una vista indicizzata e filtrabile dell'intero catalogo documentale:
- **Parametri Query opzionali**:
  - `type`: filtra per tipo di risorsa (`knowledge`, `github_repo`, `mcp_server`, `ai_skill`, `article`).
  - `tag`: filtra per etichetta specifica (es. `tag=agents`).
  - `q`: ricerca testuale libera su titolo, abstract e dominio.
- **Formato di Risposta**:
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "totalAvailable": 106,
  "matchedCount": 1,
  "resources": [
    {
      "id": "res-1725441234",
      "title": "Protocolli Operativi per Agenti Autonomi (AGENTS.md)",
      "type": "knowledge",
      "summary": "Regole di ingaggio e protocolli di esecuzione per agenti AI...",
      "tags": ["agents", "okf-v0.2", "rules"],
      "domain": "Software Architecture & AI",
      "docType": "specification",
      "entities": [...],
      "relations": [...],
      "rawUrl": "/api/vault/resources/res-1725441234/raw"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### B. Download Diretto del Markdown Puro OKF v0.2 (`GET /api/vault/resources/:id/raw`)
Restituisce il documento in formato testuale nativo `text/markdown; charset=utf-8`, corredato del frontmatter YAML completo:
```bash
# Esempio di interrogazione via cURL da parte di un agente CLI
curl -s "https://[APP_URL]/api/vault/resources/res-1725441234/raw" > context.md
```
Questo consente a qualsiasi script di automatizzazione di alimentare direttamente la finestra di contesto (*context window*) di un modello linguistico con documentazione tecnica validata e priva di sovrastrutture HTML.

#### C. Esportazione Massiva Completa (`GET /api/vault/backup`)
Restituisce l'intero database ontologico in formato JSON con metadati, entità, relazioni e testi Markdown, utile per sincronizzazioni massive, backup offline e pipeline RAG esterne.

---

### 3.2 Integrazione con Model Context Protocol (MCP)

Il Knowledge Vault include il supporto nativo per l'ecosistema **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**:
- Il Vault cataloga configurazioni e definizioni di server MCP (`mcp_server`), fornendo comandi di avvio (`stdio`/`sse`) e snippet pronti per `claude_desktop_config.json` o `.mcp.json`.
- Qualsiasi agente conforme a MCP (come Claude Desktop o Claude Code) può registrare un tool bridge che interroga l'endpoint `/api/vault/resources`, esponendo strumenti nativi nel reasoning loop dell'agente:
  - `vault_search(query: string, tag?: string)`
  - `vault_get_document(id: string)`
  - `vault_list_relations(id: string)`

---

### 3.3 Context Injection Diretto nei Prompt degli Agenti

Poiché ogni documento esportato o recuperato dal Vault adotta la sintassi standard **OKF v0.2**, i modelli linguistici (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Gemini 3.7 Flash, GPT-4o) riconoscono immediatamente:
1. **I confini semantici**: delimitati dal blocco YAML iniziale.
2. **Il ruolo e il tipo del documento**: grazie al campo `type` (`guide`, `specification`, `architecture`, `prompt_skill`).
3. **Le dipendenze ontologiche**: grazie alla sezione `relations`, che indica chiaramente al modello quali altri concetti governano o completano la specifica in esame.

---

### 3.4 Sincronizzazione con Google Drive e NotebookLM

Attraverso l'integrazione Google Drive, i documenti del Vault possono essere esportati e mantenuti allineati all'interno della cartella cloud `knowledge`:
- Strumenti come **Google NotebookLM** possono caricare l'intera cartella Drive come fonte primaria, fornendo una chat interattiva con citazioni di pagina su tutto il corpus documentale.
- Agenti provvisti di connettori Google Workspace (tramite OAuth) possono effettuare ricerche e citazioni in tempo reale senza accedere direttamente all'infrastruttura del server.

---

## 4. Matrice Riassuntiva di Accesso

| Metodo di Consultazione | Destinatario Principale | Formato Dati | Latenza | Meccanismo |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Knowledge Reader & Graph** | Utente umano, Prompt Engineer | HTML5 / D3 Canvas | 0ms (client) | Web UI Interattiva |
| **Endpoint REST Raw (`/raw`)** | Agenti CLI, cURL, Script Python | Markdown + YAML | ~50ms | HTTP GET `text/markdown` |
| **Endpoint REST List (`/resources`)** | Toolchain, Agentic Workflows | JSON OKF v0.2 | ~30ms | HTTP GET `application/json` |
| **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** | Claude Desktop, Claude Code | JSON-RPC / MCP Tools | Sub-second | Tool calling nativo |
| **Google Drive / NotebookLM** | Modelli multimodali, RAG | Google Docs / PDF | Asincrono | Sincronizzazione Cloud |
| **Filesystem Locale (`data/`)** | Agenti container interni | JSON / Snapshot | 0ms | I/O su filesystem disco |

---

## 5. Linee Guida per gli Ingegneri del Prompt

Quando si prepara un prompt per un agente autonomo basandosi sui documenti del Vault:
1. **Preferire il recupero mirato**: utilizzare `/api/vault/resources?type=specification` per estrarre solo le specifiche pertinenti al task, riducendo l'inquinamento del contesto.
2. **Conservare il Frontmatter YAML**: non eliminare il blocco `--- okf_version: "0.2" ... ---`, poiché fornisce all'agente indicazioni deterministiche sulla gerarchia concettuale.
3. **Seguire le Relazioni Ontologiche**: se un documento ha una relazione `governs` verso un altro file, è buona prassi allegare entrambi i documenti nel prompt dell'agente.

Utilizza il parsing AST locale e deterministico per fornire un contesto di progetto completo agli assistenti di coding AI, distinguendosi per l'assenza di vector store e la capacità di tracciare le relazioni con precisione. Funziona come una "skill" /graphify per oltre 20 piattaforme AI, migliorando significativamente la comprensione e l'interrogazione del codice.

Generare il grafo di conoscenza per una propria codebase usando /graphify . nel proprio assistente AI ed esplorare l'output graph.html.

aiKeyTakeaways: Approccio non-vettoriale: Costruisce un vero grafo di conoscenza attraversabile senza l'uso di embeddings o vector store, a differenza delle soluzioni RAG tradizionali.
Parsing locale e deterministico: Analizza il codice sorgente tramite AST (tree-sitter) in locale, garantendo privacy, determinismo e nessuna dipendenza da LLM per questa fase.
Contesto progettuale omnicomprensivo: Integra non solo il codice, ma anche documentazione (PDF, Markdown), configurazioni, schemi SQL, immagini e video in un unico grafo.

Interrogabilità avanzata: Permette di spiegare concetti, tracciare percorsi tra entità e porre domande in linguaggio naturale, con ogni connessione etichettata come EXTRACTED (esplicita) o INFERRED (dedotta).
Ampia compatibilità AI: Si integra facilmente come "skill" /graphify con oltre 20 assistenti di coding AI, tra cui Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot CLI e Gemini CLI.
Output ricco di informazioni: Genera graph.html (grafo navigabile), GRAPHREPORT.md (concetti chiave) e graph.json (il grafo completo interrogabile).

**Early access to the graphify platform is open before the public v1 launch: [app.graphify.com](https://app.graphify.com/login)**

Type `/graphify` in your AI coding assistant and it maps your entire project (code, docs, PDFs, images, videos) into a **knowledge graph** you can **query instead of grepping** through files.

- **Code maps for free, fully local.** Code is parsed with tree-sitter AST: deterministic, no LLM, nothing leaves your machine. (Docs, PDFs, images and video use your assistant's model, or a configured API key, for a semantic pass.)

- **Every edge is explained.** Each connection is tagged `EXTRACTED` (explicit in the source) or `INFERRED` (resolved by graphify), so you can tell what was read directly from what was inferred.

- **Not a vector index.** No embeddings, no vector store: a real graph you traverse. Ask a question, trace the path between two things, or explain one concept.

**

Want this always-on, updating in the background across your code, docs, and meetings rather than only on demand? That is what we are building at **[graphify.com](https://graphify.com)**, and early access is open now at **[app.graphify.com](https://app.graphify.com/login)**.

[ ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/v8/docs/graph-hero.png)

*The FastAPI codebase mapped by graphify. Every node is a concept, colors are detected communities, and the whole thing is clickable in graph.html.*

**Get started** (30 seconds):

uv tool install graphifyy        #  install the CLI (or: pipx install graphifyy)
graphify install                 #  register the skill with your AI assistant
Then, in your AI assistant:

`/graphify .
`
That's it. You get **three files**:

`graphify-out/
├── graph.html       open in any browser — click nodes, filter, search
├── GRAPH_REPORT.md  the highlights: key concepts, surprising connections, suggested questions
└── graph.json       the full graph — query it anytime without re-reading your files
`
**Works in** Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, and 15+ more — [pick your platform](#install).

---

## See it in action

[ ](#see-it-in-action)

[ ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/v8/docs/demo-path.svg)

Once the graph is built you query it instead of reading files. Real output, graphify run on the FastAPI codebase shown above:

`$ graphify explain "APIRouter"
Node: APIRouter
Source:    routing.py L2210
Community: 2
Degree:    47

Connections (47):
--> RequestValidationError [uses] [INFERRED]
--> Dependant [uses] [INFERRED]
--> .get() [method] [EXTRACTED]
<-- __init__.py [imports] [EXTRACTED]
...

$ graphify path "FastAPI" "ModelField"
Shortest path (3 hops):
FastAPI --uses--> DefaultPlaceholder <--references-- get_request_handler() --references--> ModelField
`
Every edge carries a **confidence tag** (`EXTRACTED` = explicit in the source, `INFERRED` = derived by resolution), so you can tell what was read directly from what was inferred. `graphify query "<question>"` returns a scoped subgraph for a plain-language question, and `graphify path A B` traces how any two things connect.

---

## What it does

[ ](#what-it-does)

What you get out of the box:

**God nodes**
The most-connected concepts, so you see what everything flows through

**Communities**
The graph split into subsystems (Leiden), with LLM-free labels

**Cross-file links**
`calls` / `imports` / `inherits` / `mixes_in` resolved across ~40 languages via tree-sitter AST

**Query, path, explain**
Ask a question, trace the path between two things, or explain one concept, all against `graph.json`

**Rationale + doc refs**
`# NOTE:` / `# WHY:` comments and ADR/RFC citations become first-class nodes linked to the code

**Beyond code**
Docs, PDFs, images, and video/audio all map into the same graph

**Local-first**
Code is parsed locally with tree-sitter (no LLM, nothing leaves your machine); only the semantic pass over docs/media calls a backend, and only if you configure one

## Install

[ ](#install)

>
**Official package:** The PyPI package is `graphifyy` (double-y). Other `graphify*` packages on PyPI are not affiliated. The CLI command is still `graphify`.

**Step 1 — install the package:**

#  Recommended (isolated env; if 'graphify' isn't found after, run: uv tool update-shell):
uv tool install graphifyy

#  Alternatives:
pipx install graphifyy
pip install graphifyy    #  may need PATH setup — see note below
**Step 2 — register the skill with your AI assistant:**

graphify install
That's it. Open your AI assistant and type `/graphify .`

To install the assistant skill into the current repository instead of your user
profile, add `--project`:

graphify install --project
graphify install --project --platform codex
Project-scoped installs write under the current directory, for example
`.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` or `.agents/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` (plus a
`references/` sidecar the skill loads on demand), and
print a `git add` hint for files that can be committed.
Per-platform commands that support project-scoped installs accept the same flag,
for example `graphify claude install --project` or `graphify codex install --project`.

>

**PowerShell note:** Use `graphify .` not `/graphify .` — the leading slash is a path separator in PowerShell.

>

**`graphify: command not found`?** `uv tool install` / `pipx install` put the `graphify` command in their tool bin dir (`~/.local/bin`). If your shell can't find it right after install — common on a fresh macOS + zsh setup — that dir isn't on your `PATH` yet: run `uv tool update-shell` (or `pipx ensurepath`), then open a new terminal. With plain `pip`, add `~/.local/bin` (Linux) or `~/Library/Python/3.x/bin` (Mac) to your PATH, or run `python -m graphify`.

>

**Running with `uvx` / `uv tool run` instead of installing?** Name the package, not the command: `uvx --from graphifyy graphify install`. Plain `uvx graphify …` fails (`No solution found … no versions of graphify`) because `uv tool run` reads the first word as a *package*, and the package is `graphifyy` — the `graphify` command lives inside it.

>

**Avoid `pip install` on Mac/Windows** if possible. The skill resolves Python at runtime from `graphify-out/.graphify_python`; if that points to a different environment than where `pip` installed the package, you'll get `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'graphify'`. `uv tool install` and `pipx install` isolate the package in their own env and avoid this entirely.

>

**Git hooks and uv tool / pipx:** `graphify hook install` embeds the current interpreter path directly into the hook scripts at install time, so the post-commit hook fires correctly even in GUI git clients and CI runners where `~/.local/bin` is not on PATH. If you reinstall or upgrade graphify, re-run `graphify hook install` to refresh the embedded path.

>

**Strict mode (Claude Code):** `graphify install --project --strict` makes the assistant actually use the graph. The default install *nudges* it to run `graphify query` before reading files; strict mode *blocks* the first raw source read of a session and redirects it to the graph, then reverts to the nudge (so it fires at most once per session and never gets stuck). Toggle at runtime with `GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT=1`/`0`; the default install is unchanged (soft nudge).
